scope.description: Ten cases in one execution over three real OmniPaxos instances in one process with MemoryStorage and a deterministic FIFO in-process network; the new case drives the drift, changes the leader, compacts the new leader past a live replica's reported accepted index and then lets that replica re-synchronize, reporting any panic as an event field rather than aborting the run.
assumptions: Entry type Value has Snapshot = NoSnapshot; ClusterConfig { configuration_id: 1, nodes: [1,2,3], flexible_quorum: None } with default ServerConfig (batch_size 1); BLE messages are dropped, as in the lineage.

Three rounds of node1.reconnected(3) plus node2.reconnected(3) reproduce the drifted state (followers accepted 9, leader decided 9 over six indices of content); node1.try_become_leader() then makes node 1 the leader and re-synchronizes the other two, which in the lineage left node 3 at accepted 7 against the drifted decided index.

The snapshot is requested with the leader's own decided index as the bound and local_only = true, so no Compaction message is sent to the peers and the compacted index becomes that decided index (the StopSign is no longer counted as decided in the drifted state, so the bound is not lowered).

reconnected(pid) is called with the current leader, because the library only starts a re-synchronization when the peer named is the leader; every drain and sample runs inside catch_unwind, so a panic inside a handler becomes an event field instead of aborting the run.
excluded: No entry type with use_snapshots() true is used in the new case, so the snapshot branch of create_log_sync is not exercised there.
No load, timer, message loss or node restart is exercised; only reconnected() calls and one leader change.
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.

parameters.compaction_bound: the new leader's own decided index at the time of the call

basis.prefix: Same prefix as the lineage: node 3 leads, five entries are appended and decided, then a StopSign is proposed with reconfigure() and decided, so every node holds six indices of content and reports accepted 6 / decided 6 (OVER_BASE). The new case then performs three rounds of node1.reconnected(3)+node2.reconnected(3), each drained and sampled per node as OVER_R{k}_N{pid} for k = 1..3, reads the leader's decided index, elects node 1 with try_become_leader() and samples as OVER_AFTER_CHANGE, calls node1.snapshot(Some(decided), true) and emits OVER_SNAP with the outcome, the panicked flag, the compacted index, the accepted index and the decided index of the leader, then calls node3.reconnected(1) (the replica whose reported accepted index is below the compacted index) with a guarded drain and samples, emits OVER_LAG_RESULT with the panicked flag, repeats the same for node2.reconnected(1) as the control and emits OVER_AHEAD_RESULT, and finally emits OVER_RUN_END with the number of messages delivered. Every sample records accepted_idx, decided_idx, decided_eq_accepted, is_reconfigured, the read of index 5, the read of index 6, the read of the decided suffix from 0 and its length.

comparisons.description: The snapshot call that compacts the leader inside its drifted decided index completes on its own without panicking.

The re-synchronization of the replica whose reported accepted index lies below the compacted index is handled without a panic: no handler may be brought down by a prefix request below the compacted index.

Control: the replica whose reported accepted index is at or above the compacted index re-synchronizes without a panic, so any panic in the other stage is not attributable to re-synchronization as such.

before.description: Nine cases in one execution over three real OmniPaxos instances in one process with MemoryStorage and a deterministic FIFO in-process network; the new case keeps the lineage prefix and then re-synchronizes the two followers eight further times, replaces the leader with one of those inflated followers, and re-synchronizes the remaining replicas three more times against the new leader, sampling all three nodes every round and reporting any handler panic as an event field rather than aborting the run.
assumptions: Entry type Value has Snapshot = NoSnapshot; ClusterConfig { configuration_id: 1, nodes: [1,2,3], flexible_quorum: None } with default ServerConfig (batch_size 1); BLE messages are dropped, as in the lineage.

A round is node1.reconnected(3) plus node2.reconnected(3) followed by a drain of the queue; after the leader change the followers report the new leader, i.e. node2.reconnected(1) plus node3.reconnected(1), because reconnected(pid) only triggers a re-synchronization when pid is the current leader.

AcceptSync/Promise traffic is generated by the library itself; the harness only supplies the re-established connections and drains the queue, so the resume points are the library's own reported accepted indexes.

catch_unwind wraps each round's drain together with that round's samples, and separately the leader change, so a panic inside a handler or inside a storage read becomes the BOUND_STAGES.panics count; it does not change protocol behaviour when no panic occurs.
excluded: No entry type with use_snapshots() true is used in the new case, and no compaction is requested in it, so trim and snapshot over-compaction are out of this case's scope.
No node restart, storage loss, timers or message loss are exercised; only the reconnected() path and the ordinary leader-change path.
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.
